hero.h1: Roofing Company in Wichita, KS — Ashbrook Roofing & Contracting
hero.sub: I'm Andy Ashbrook. I replace and repair roofs in Wichita, and when insurance is part of the job I work through the claim with you. Call me or request an estimate, and I'll look at your roof before you decide anything.

sections.quote: From our first meeting, Andy was not pushy and very attentive to our questions and requests!
sections.name: Chef L.

sections.heading: One Person Answers for Your Roof
body: A roof job has a lot of pieces: the first look, the quote, the insurance, the crew, the cleanup. Too often you end up carrying the details from one person to the next.
With us it's me. I come out and look at the roof, write the quote, and send the crew that does the work. If a claim is involved, I'm in that conversation too.
You don't need to learn roofing to get this right. You need one person who explains what's on your roof and stays in the job until it's finished.

sections.quote: Andy made replacing our roof as painless as possible! We genuinely felt as though he had our best interests at heart, and he made sure we were well-informed throughout the process.
sections.name: Maureen S.

sections.heading: When Insurance Is Part of the Job
body: A storm goes through. Maybe there's a stain on the ceiling, maybe the roof looks fine from the driveway, and you've never filed a claim in your life.
An adjuster walks your roof for a short visit, and what goes in the report shapes the whole job. The photos, the notes and the list of what's damaged all matter.
That's the part I do with you. I look at the roof, document what I find, and explain it in plain words. When your adjuster comes out, I'll be there if you want me there.

If the first answer from the insurance company looks short, I'll help you ask for a second look. Your policy and your decisions stay yours, and no roofer can tell you what an insurance company will pay.

sections.quote: Andy offered to come out when the insurance adjuster was there to help us through the insurance process.
sections.name: Jan S.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement
body: Some roofs are done. Shingles curl at the edges, granules pile up at the bottom of your downspouts, and leaks show up in more than one place. At that point, patching only buys you a season.
We tear off the old roof and look at the deck underneath before anything new goes down. Many of our roofs go on in a single day, so you're not living under a tarp for a week.
If your gutters are worn out or took the same storm, we can replace them in the same job. That's one crew and one schedule.

sections.quote: They re-roofed our entire house and garage in a single day! Everything was clean and tidy when we got home!
sections.name: Denton C.

sections.heading: Roof Repair
body: Plenty of roofs don't need replacing. A few shingles blew off in the wind, a vent leaks, or there's a spot on the ceiling that comes back after every rain.
Water rarely comes through the roof right above the stain. It runs along the deck and drops somewhere else, so I look for where it gets in, not just where you see it.
When a repair is enough, I'll tell you that. When it isn't, I'll show you why.

sections.heading: Clean When We Leave
body: A new roof means a crew walking your yard, dropping old shingles and nails. Where your car parks and your kids play matters as much as the roof.
We protect the landscaping before the work starts, and we pick up nails and material before we go.

sections.quote: Andy's crew made sure everything was cleaned up and protected all of the landscaping from damage!
sections.name: Richard M.

sections.heading: Gutters, Siding and the Rest of the Exterior
body: The roof is the biggest job, but it isn't the only one. The work around it is often what finishes the house.
list: **Gutters:** replaced along with the roof, or on their own when they're worn out or damaged.
**Siding:** repaired or replaced, often after the same storm that hit the roof.
**Soffit and fascia:** the boards under and along the roof edge.
**Interior remodeling:** some, when it goes with the work on your house.
tail: If it's part of the outside of your house, ask. I'll tell you if it's something we do.

sections.heading: Selling Your House on a Deadline
body: A roof can turn up in an inspection a week before closing. I've handled roofs for people selling houses, and I know the schedule can't slip.
If that's you, call me with the closing date. I'll look at the roof quickly and tell you what's realistic.
I also work with real estate agents who send me clients. If you're an agent with a house that has a roof problem, call me directly.

body: I'm in Wichita and I work on Wichita roofs. If you're outside the city, call and tell me where you are.

items.q: Do you help with insurance claims?
items.a: Yes. I document the roof, come out when the adjuster is there, and help you ask for a second look if the first answer looks short. What the insurance company pays is between you and them.

items.q: Will insurance pay for a new roof?
items.a: It depends on your policy and on what the adjuster finds. I can't promise an outcome, and anyone who does is guessing.

items.q: How long does a roof take?

hero.h1: Roof Replacement in Wichita, KS — Ashbrook Roofing & Contracting
hero.sub: When a roof is finished, you shouldn't have to sort out the claim, the crew and the schedule by yourself. I'm Andy, and I handle all three. Call me or request an estimate, and I'll tell you honestly whether the roof needs replacing.

sections.heading: How You Know It's Time
body: A roof doesn't fail all at once. It gives you signs, and most of them can be seen from the yard.

Shingles curl up at the edges or crack across the middle. Granules, the rough gritty coating, wash down into your gutters and collect at the bottom of the downspouts. Leaks show up in more than one place.
One bad spot is a repair. Wear across the whole roof is a replacement, and patching it just means paying twice.
Hail changes the picture. It bruises shingles where you can't see it from the ground, and a roof that looks fine can leak a couple of years later.
If you're not sure which one you have, I'll go up and look. If it's only a repair, I'll tell you, and you can read about [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/).

sections.heading: What Replacement Day Looks Like
body: The crew shows up early. Landscaping gets protected first, and then the old roof comes off.
With the old shingles gone, we look at the deck underneath. Soft or stained wood needs replacing, not covering, because a new roof on a weak surface hides the problem until it fails.
Then the underlayment, flashing and vents go in, and the new shingles go on. Many of our roofs are finished in a single day.
Before the crew leaves, the yard gets checked for nails and material.

sections.quote: They got it done in under 7hrs! All the crew was friendly & Andy the owner was very easy to work with & made the whole process seamless & easy.
sections.name: James R.

sections.heading: When the Weather Changes the Plan
body: Roofs depend on the weather, and Kansas weather doesn't keep a schedule. A roof shouldn't be torn off ahead of rain.
I watch the forecast. If the date has to move, I move it and let you know.

sections.quote: We got rained out on the originally scheduled replacement date and he was able to quickly pivot to get my roof replaced in a matter of days. The crew also did great work and cleaned up great leaving no nails or material behind.
sections.name: Kyle W.

sections.heading: Replacement With an Insurance Claim
body: When a storm is what finished your roof, a replacement comes with a claim. That means photos, an adjuster's visit and a scope of work, with paperwork in between.
I document the roof and explain what I find in plain words. When the adjuster comes out, I'll be there if you want me there.

If the first answer looks short, I'll help you ask the insurance company to take a second look. It's your policy and your decision. I don't promise what an insurance company will pay, because no roofer can.

sections.quote: We had fought with our insurance company for nearly a year without any success. Andy worked with us and guided us through the process of requesting a reevaluation of our claim. He was available and responsive when we had questions throughout the process.
sections.name: Emily H.

sections.heading: A Roof on a Deadline
body: Sometimes the roof is the thing standing between you and a closing. An inspection turns it up, and suddenly you have days, not months.
Call me with the date. I'll tell you what's realistic, and I'll work with your agent and the insurance company so the roof isn't the reason a sale falls apart.

sections.quote: Andy showed up and inspected the roof to confirm and had it marked for the insurance photos within an hour of calling him. He worked with the adjuster and I had a new roof scheduled for the buyers before we closed that day.
sections.name: Steven A.

sections.heading: Roof and Gutters Together
body: The gutters sit right at the roof edge, so they take the same storm the shingles do. They also wear out on the same schedule.
If yours are worn, dented or pulling away, replacing them in the same job saves a second crew and a second schedule. It also keeps a ladder off your brand-new roof edge.

sections.quote: Andy took care of replacing my roof and gutters without any problems. Very easy to work with! Will use again.
sections.name: Shane K.

list: The size of the roof, and how steep it is.
How many layers of old shingles are on it.
The condition of the deck once the old roof is off.
Flashing, vents and anything that has to be redone around chimneys or skylights.

hero.h1: Roof Repair in Wichita, KS — Ashbrook Roofing & Contracting
hero.sub: A few shingles blew off, or a leak showed up and you can't tell where it starts. I'm Andy, and I'll find where the water gets in and fix that, not just the spot on your ceiling. Call me or request an estimate, and I'll tell you straight whether it's a repair or something bigger.

sections.heading: Shingles Blown Off in the Wind
body: You come home after a windy night and there are shingles in the yard, or you spot a bare patch from the street. A missing shingle exposes the layer under it, and that layer was never made to sit in the sun and rain.
Wind gets under the edge of a shingle whose seal has aged, and lifts it. Once one goes, the shingles next to it are easier to lift.
We replace what blew off, look over the shingles around it and make sure the new ones seal down. That's usually a small job, and it's best done before the next storm.

sections.heading: A Leak Isn't Always Where the Stain Is
body: Water doesn't drop straight down. It enters the roof in one place, runs along the deck or a rafter, and shows up as a stain a few feet away.
That's why patching right above the stain so often fails. The leak is still there, and the stain comes back.
The usual entry points are flashing, the metal around chimneys, walls and vents, along with pipe boots and valleys. A bead of caulk can hide a bad flashing job for a season, but it doesn't fix one.
I start at the stain and work up and out until I find where the water gets in. Then I fix that.

sections.quote: We called Ashbrook roofing after we noticed a small leak in our roof following a spring storm. The team was out here the same day to assess the situation. Not only did they find the leak, but they also noticed that our vents were out of code and our gutters were beyond their lifespan.
sections.name: Jordan W.

sections.heading: Skylights, Vents and Other Places Roofs Leak
body: Anything that goes through a roof is a place for water to get in. That's skylights, vent pipes, chimneys and the joints where one roof meets a wall.
Skylights age out. The seal around the frame dries, cracks or pulls loose, and the leak looks like a roof problem when it isn't.
When one of these is the cause, that's where the fix goes, not in the shingles around it.

sections.quote: His professional team are truly skilled and thorough. They spent extra effort to ensure my aging skylights were well sealed.
sections.name: Ben W.

sections.heading: Looking Past the Spot You Pointed To
body: You called about one thing. A roof rarely has just one thing.

While I'm up there, I look at the shingles around the damage, the vents, the flashing and the gutter edge. Older shingles go brittle, and the ones next to a problem tell me how much life the roof has left.
If I see something else, I show you and explain it. Then you decide.

sections.quote: Andy took his time to explain all the small details that other companies passed over. He noticed the small things and had it fixed without me having to do anything!
sections.name: Johna F.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace? I'll Tell You Honestly
body: A repair makes sense when the damage is in one place and the rest of the roof is sound. Replacement makes sense when the trouble is everywhere: shingles curling across several slopes, granules piling up in the gutters, leaks in more than one spot.
If your roof is just old and worn, I'll say so. I'd rather tell you a repair will hold than sell you a roof you don't need.

sections.quote: We had storm damage to our roof in a few places. They were able to repair it quicky. Andy was honest about what I needed, and I appreciate that the most.
sections.name: Scott B.

body: When replacement is the honest answer, here's how [a full roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) goes.

sections.heading: Storm Damage and Insurance
body: If a storm caused the damage, the repair may be part of a claim. I'll tell you what I see on the roof and explain how the process works.
I don't promise what an insurance company will pay, and I won't tell you to file a claim you don't need. It's your policy and your decision.

items.title: I come out.
items.text: I go up on the roof and look at more than the spot you pointed to.

items.title: I tell you what I found.
items.text: You get the repair and the reason for it before any work starts.

items.title: The work gets done.
items.text: A small repair is usually quick.

items.title: We clean up.
items.text: Nothing gets left in your yard.

items.q: How soon should I fix missing shingles?
items.a: As soon as you reasonably can. The layer underneath isn't made to face the weather, and the next wind or rain makes it worse.

items.q: Why is my ceiling stained when the roof looks fine?
items.a: Water often travels from where it enters. Flashing, vent boots, skylights and valleys are the first places I check.

items.q: Will a repair match my old shingles?
items.a: Close, usually, but not perfectly. Sun fades shingles, so new ones can look a shade different at first.
Yes. Gutters are part of the roof edge, and I'll look at them while I'm there.
